tech.label: GSAP feature
sort.label: Sort
sort.name: Name
costNote.transform: Only transforms and opacity, handled by the GPU — almost free.
costNote.layout: Animates width or height, so layout is recalculated every frame. Fine for a few elements; don’t do it to a whole page.
costNote.blur: filter: blur repaints every frame; large areas can drop frames on low-end phones. Keep it to short text and small areas.
costNote.blurOnce: The blur plays once on load and then stops, but many large images at once cost briefly.
costNote.scroll: Updates every scroll frame, but only transforms, so it stays smooth.
costNote.pin: Pinning wraps the section and changes layout. One or two per page is fine; many add up.
costNote.clip: clip-path repaints the clipped area each frame — a moderate cost for large or full-screen images.
costNote.pointer: Updates on every pointer move, but quickTo reuses one tween, so it’s light.
costNote.ticker: Every frame measures each element against the cursor (gsap.ticker); fine for a few hundred elements, switch to canvas for thousands. The loop stops when nothing is moving.
costNote.mask: The mask (a mask-image gradient) repaints every frame as the cursor moves; smooth over a modest area, a medium cost full-screen.
costNote.flip3d: 3D flips only touch transform, but with many two-sided tiles flipping at once, watch it past a hundred or so.
costNote.flip: Flip measures layout once at the start, then only animates transforms; you’d only notice with hundreds of elements.
costNote.svg: Only stroke-dashoffset changes; light with a few paths.
costNote.loop: Loops forever; pause it when it scrolls off-screen.
costNote.particles: Creates a dozen particle elements and removes them afterwards; fine at that scale.
costNote.drag: Dragging and the glide afterwards only move transforms — light.
costNote.3d: 3D rotation is cheap, but the glare gradient repaints every frame; watch out with many cards on one page.
costNote.text: Splitting creates many elements; fine for headings, heavier for long paragraphs.
costNote.path: Computes positions along a path for a single element — light.
costNote.paint: The shine moves via background-position, which repaints every frame; fine for a few blocks, but for a whole page move a pseudo-element with transform instead.

guide.title: Motion guidelines
guide.lead: The judgement built up while making these practices: which ease, how long, when GSAP is worth it and how to keep it cheap. Every rule links to the practices that use it.
guide.durNote: Exits are quicker than entrances: the same component leaves in roughly 60–70% of its entrance time.
lab.title: Ease lab
lab.lead: Pick an ease, tune its parameters and duration, and watch the curve, four properties and a side-by-side race. Then copy it as GSAP or CSS. The URL keeps your settings, so you can share it.
lab.graphLabel: Ease curve: time across, progress up
lab.compareEmpty: Add the current ease, switch to another and press play to see which arrives first and which feels more urgent. Up to 4.
lab.copyFailed: Couldn’t copy. Select the text and copy it manually.
lab.cssBezier: The CSS is an approximate cubic-bezier: very close to GSAP’s curve, but not identical.
lab.cssLinear: This curve can’t be a cubic-bezier, so it’s sampled with CSS linear(); older browsers don’t support it.
